dish: clam & broad-bean-tofu owan in Rishiri-kelp/bonito dashi with house-made ishiri; char-grilled cherry salmon
w: Chef Hiroshi Kawaguchi's kaiseki counter near Kyōbashi, reopened under this name in 2023; awarded One MICHELIN Star in the Michelin Guide Kyoto Osaka 2025.

dish: goat dishes air-freighted from Miyakojima (hijāgusui goat soup, goat sashimi) and 48-hour-simmered sōki soba
n: Okinawa Sakaba Kijimunā no Mori (沖縄酒場 きじむなーの森)
address: Sangenya-nishi, Taishō-ku, Osaka (moved into TUGBOAT_TAISHO, 1-11-14 Sangenya-nishi, Jan 2020)
w: Long-loved Little Okinawa izakaya from under the Taishō rail viaduct, relocated into TUGBOAT_TAISHO in January 2020 (Lmaga.jp); featured in Kansai Walker's Taishō Little Okinawa guide.

dish: Korean reimen (cold noodles) with house-made kimchi on every table; kimchi bibimbap & kimchi-jjigae
n: Yamada Shōten (山田商店, Ikuno Koreatown)
w: 40-plus-year handmade-kimchi shop in Ikuno Koreatown (~80 kinds) that opened an eatery in Oct 2022; Rurubu's Tsuruhashi Korea Town food crawl and Inside Osaka both single out its cheap reimen.

dish: momi-dare beef — no dipping sauce; each cut massaged in marinade to order (shio-tan, bara, jō-mino)
n: Yakiniku Horumon Manmasa (焼肉・ホルモン 万正)
w: Tsuruhashi-area yakiniku/horumon house that seasons each order with momi-dare tuned to the day's meat instead of a dipping sauce; newly selected for Tabelog Yakiniku WEST Hyakumeiten 2025 and listed by Mapple's guidebook editors.

dish: mimigā sashimi and umi-budō with a list of ~150 awamori
n: Omoro Taishō Honten (おもろ 大正本店)
w: Pioneer of Osaka's Okinawan izakaya, opened ~30 years ago a short walk from JR Taishō Station (Kansai Walker's Little Okinawa guide); Mapple's guidebook editors note ~60 Okinawan dishes and ~150 awamori.

dish: ¥300 oden moriawase and ¥500 fresh otsukuri platter with sake poured at liquor-shop prices
n: Okamuro Saketen Chokubaijo (岡室酒店直売所, Kyōbashi)
w: Liquor-store-run standing bar on Kyōbashi's 'tachinomi street', open from 9am; featured in Nakajima Ramo's 'Senbero Tantei ga Iku' (Kansai Walker) and listed by Mapple's guidebook editors as Kyōbashi's oasis.
